meta.purpose: Authoritative, machine-parseable task inventory for the full simulation/feature-coverage loop. Drive four engines (CanDo FEM, mrDNA, oxDNA, NAMD) to cover the four unconventional design features (extra crossover bases, linkers/overhang connections, E-fields, anchors) AND emit a shared, comparable set of prediction descriptors so engines cross-validate each other.
meta.reference_policy: per-observable: oxDNA is reference for relaxed shape + field-deflection; CanDo is reference for RMSF/flexibility; NAMD becomes gold for any observable once a NAMD run for that design exists (overrides).
meta.loop_invariant: The loop edits ONLY task.status and task.notes (and milestone.status, derived). It MUST NOT add, remove, reorder, or rewrite tasks, deps, oracles, or any other field. Scope changes, new tasks, or re-prioritization require the user. Seeded all-pending on purpose (nothing is 'done' until its oracle passes).
meta.three_layer_law: Every engine output here is PHYSICAL/display-only. Anchors + field specs are JOB-REQUEST annotations, never Design edits. CanDo extra-base/linker ELEMENTS are mesh-build details derived from existing topology metadata (Crossover.extra_bases, overhang_connections), not topology mutations.

tasks.title: E-field: add uniform q*E per-node nodal load to the assemble_prestress_force vector (editable effective-charge const, same convention as oxDNA); predict_shape(design, field=..., anchors=...); nonlinear solve for large deflections
tasks.oracle: FAST: shared measure_field_response (S4) on the FEM deflected frame -> anchor holds, free deflects along field, deflection monotone in field magnitude, zero-field -> no deflection. SLOW: nonlinear field solve on a tethered-arm fixture.
tasks.notes: Uniform E-field body load for the CanDo FEM (backend-only; field is a JOB-REQUEST annotation like anchors, never a Design/topology edit -- Three-Layer Law). assemble_field_force(mesh, field) builds the equivalent nodal-force vector from the shared oxDNA descriptor {"field_pN":<force per NUCLEOTIDE, pN>, "dir":[x,y,z]} -- the SAME per-nucleotide force oxDNA applies per bead (OXDNA_FORCE_PN convention). Each duplex axis node carries FEM_FIELD_CHARGES_PER_NODE=2 backbones, so its translational load is 2*field_pN*dir_hat (pN), rotational DOF zero (a pure body force, no couple). None/{}/zero-mag/zero-dir -> exact zero vector; magnitude linear. The field is a DEAD load: assembled ONCE in global coords before the corotational loop and added to the per-step-reframed eigenstrain each of n_steps increments, so it stays fixed in the lab frame as the bundle bends (unlike the co-rotating loop/skip eigenstrain). Threaded through solve_prestress_shape(...,field=) (nonlinear) + predict_shape(design,*,anchors=,field=) both paths; a field needs >=1 anchor to hold against (COM drift), reusing C1 resolve_anchor_nodes. ORACLE = shared S4 shape_metrics.field_response_profile on the FEM deflected frame vs the same design field-OFF frame, measured on the RAW solved axis-node positions -- NOT predict_shape display positions, which are per-frame Kabsch-REPOSED onto the design (deformed_positions_with_axis) so straight(ref)+bent(cand) land in different poses and the anchor would spuriously drift ~5nm; the raw clamped-solve frame is a genuine common frame (6 end nodes fully constrain rigid body). tests/test_cando_field.py 7: assemble_field_force unit props (none/zero no-op, 2*chg/node translational-only direction, linear magnitude) FAST; end-to-end (anchored 6HB, transverse field) anchors held (drift ~0) + free deflects ALONG field (proj>=0.5nm) + monotone in |E| (fp 0.05->5.2nm, 0.1->10.4nm) + zero-field->no deflection (RED guard) + predict_shape(field=) threads through & field=None is a byte-identical no-op -- these 4 nonlinear-solve tests registered SLOW in conftest (each multiple corotational solves), unit tests stay fast. n_steps=8 converged+stable (fp>=~0.5 blows up the corotational solve; gentle fields chosen). Fresh-context review: no correctness gaps; predict_shape public S4 verdict proven indirectly (shares the exact solve_prestress_shape(field=) the property tests validate) -- documented, inherent (S4 on the Kabsch display frame would falsely fail). Gates: 7/7 oracle, just test 4194 passed/66 skip/1 xfail, ruff clean on touched. No card/UI -> display-vs-oracle N/A (like C1). main.js LOC delta=0. Closes M-CANDO-FIELD (C1,C2,S4,S5,O1 all done): the cheap FEM now predicts the oxDNA field-deflection regime (anchored tethered-arm, deflection along field, monotone) with the SAME per-nt force convention -- the C5 field-source builder must emit field-response from the RAW frame, not predict_shape display positions.

tasks.notes: The compliant-connector MECHANISM already lived in build_fem_mesh (an extra-base crossover meshes as a 2-node WLC ssDNA spring k_trans=3*KBT/(2*L_c*L_P_SS), k_rot=0, instead of a rigid link -- CanDo CONN3D2 analogue, shipped untested in Phase-5 commit 9121b78). C3's bright-line deliverable was therefore the OMISSING property ORACLE, not new production code. New tests/test_cando_extra_bases.py (3 FAST + 1 SLOW, slow registered in conftest). FAST (deterministic): (1) census -- an extra-base crossover meshes as a compliant spring (k_rot==0, k_trans==WLC formula, <K_PENALTY/1e3) and leaves the rigid-link set; spring count == #inserted crossovers, springs+rigid conserved (mesh reflects inserts; CanDo models ssDNA as a connector between EXISTING bp nodes, so no added nodes -- 'reflects inserts' = connector TYPE, not node count); (2) k_trans softens monotonically with insert length (T>TT>TTTT, k1==2*k2, k proportional 1/L_c); (3) synthetic 2-node compliance -- under the SAME transverse load a WLC-spring crossover deflects >1e3x more than a rigid link (u==F/k_trans vs F/K_PENALTY exactly). Three-Layer clean: _with_inserts does model_copy(deep) before stamping extra_bases; solver only READS Crossover.extra_bases (never a topology mutation). tasks.notes: NAMD native uniform E-field via eFieldOn/eField (q·E on every charged atom). Backend (a JOB-REQUEST annotation, never a Design edit — Three-Layer Law): (1) md_protocols.namd_efield_vector({field_pN,dir}) converts the SHARED cross-engine descriptor (force per NUCLEOTIDE in pN — the same load oxDNA/LAMMPS apply per bead, CanDo per duplex node) to NAMD's eField vector in kcal/mol/Å/e.
